title: Proper formal systems compare with a completion up to nonzero-ideal power torsion
statement: Let $A,I,X,f,J$ be as in proper projective pullback [lem-weil-pbc-proper-existence-projective-pullback], with X nonempty, and M a coherent formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. There exist a quasi-coherent ideal K of X [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] whose every positive power is nonzero, a coherent module H [pqf-def-coherent], a map $\alpha:M\to H^\wedge$, and t at least one such that a kernel fork k and cokernel cofork c of alpha, with their limiting and colimiting universal properties, have every term annihilated by $K^t$. These universal properties are in the coherent formal category, using its zero morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. No closed-quotient algebraization assumption is made.

source.place: Proposition 30.25.4 (088C), last paragraph: the complement ideal and proper push-pull comparison, using Lemma 088B

proof.text: Get q:Y -> X, dense open U, F and the ambient pullback algebraization beta from proper_existence_projective_pullback.

Set K to Mathlib vanishingIdeal(U.compl). Its support is U.compl by coe_support_vanishingIdeal. For any e>=1, support_pow says the support of K^e is that same complement. If K^e were zero its support would be all of X by support_bot. A dense open in a nonempty space is nonempty; a point of U contradicts this equality. Also K.support.compl=U. The pullback-restriction comparison identifies pullback.snd q U.ι with an isomorphism followed by q restricted to U, hence it is an isomorphism.

Apply exists_formalSystemsPushPull to J,K,q,M,F,beta and the preceding pullback-snd isomorphism. It gives coherence of H=q_*F, alpha, t>=1, kernel fork and cokernel cofork, their universal properties, and both termwise annihilation assertions. Reassociate the existential conjunctions to match the stated torsion tuple.

mathlib_searches.query: Failure of algebraization of coherent formal modules on a proper scheme reduces to a maximal closed subscheme with every nonzero closed quotient algebraizable
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results: affine transition limits, finite morphisms, integral schemes, and a properness criterion over a field. None gives this algebraization reduction.

Library search found full faithfulness, devissage, projective existence, formal pullback, push-pull and the proved ProjectiveSpace.exists_isClosedImmersion_finite_coordinates. No maximal algebraization counterexample theorem or direct proper-existence proof. The 088E Chow comparison has a different conclusion about proper support, and is not applicable on an already proper scheme.

lean.statement: theorem proper_existence_comparison (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [Nonempty X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsProper f] (M : CoherentFormalModule X ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).ker.comap f)) : let J := (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))).ker.comap f ∃ K : X.IdealSheafData, (∀ e : ℕ, 1 ≤ e → K ^ e ≠ ⊥) ∧ ∃ (H : CoherentModules X) (α : M ⟶ (completion X J).obj H), ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∃ k : KernelFork α, ∃ c : CokernelCofork α, Nonempty (IsLimit k) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (k.pt.obj.obj (op n)))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 (c.pt.obj.obj (op n))))
